title: Nouns: Singular & Plural
rule:
SINGULAR = one thing.  PLURAL = more than one.

RULE 1 — Most nouns: add -s
   cat → cats,  book → books,  bag → bags

RULE 2 — Ends in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z: add -es
   bus → buses,  dish → dishes,  box → boxes,  watch → watches

RULE 3 — Consonant + y: change y to -ies
   baby → babies,  lady → ladies,  city → cities
   (But vowel + y just add -s: boy → boys, day → days)

RULE 4 — Some -f / -fe endings: change to -ves
   leaf → leaves,  knife → knives,  wife → wives

RULE 5 — IRREGULAR (must memorise)
   child → children,  man → men,  woman → women
   foot → feet,  tooth → teeth,  mouse → mice,  person → people

RULE 6 — Same for both
   sheep → sheep,  fish → fish,  deer → deer
ruleZh: 单数是一个，复数是多个。多数名词加 -s；以 s/sh/ch/x 结尾加 -es；辅音+y 改成 -ies；有些 f/fe 改成 -ves；有些是不规则的（child→children）。

questions.why: children is already plural, so use 'are'.

title: Nouns: Countable & Uncountable
rule:
COUNTABLE nouns — you can count them (1, 2, 3...)
   one apple, two apples, three cups
   Can be singular or plural.
   Use: a / an, many, few, a few

UNCOUNTABLE nouns — you cannot count them
   water, rice, sugar, money, advice, information, furniture, homework
   NEVER add -s.  Always treated as singular.
   Use: much, little, a little, some

HOW TO COUNT UNCOUNTABLE THINGS
   Use a container or measure word:
   a glass of water,  a bowl of rice,  a bag of sugar,  a piece of advice

QUICK TEST
   Can you say "two ___"?  →  Yes = countable.  No = uncountable.
   two apples ✅ countable
   two waters ❌ uncountable → say "two glasses of water"

COMMON MISTAKES
   ❌ many rice        ✅ much rice
   ❌ two advices      ✅ two pieces of advice
   ❌ How many money?  ✅ How much money?
ruleZh: 可数名词能数（一个苹果、两个苹果），可以有复数。不可数名词不能数（水、米、钱），永远不加 -s。可数用 many，不可数用 much。要数不可数名词就用量词：一杯水、一碗饭。

questions.why: Use a container word for uncountable nouns.

questions.q: There is ___ milk in the fridge.
There are ___ eggs in the fridge.

opts: I bought three loaves of bread.
I bought a lot of bread.

title: Pronouns
rule:
A PRONOUN replaces a noun so you don't repeat it.
   Mama cooks. Mama is happy.  →  Mama cooks. SHE is happy.

SUBJECT pronouns — do the action (before the verb)
   I, you, he, she, it, we, they
   SHE cooks dinner.   THEY are playing.

OBJECT pronouns — receive the action (after the verb)
   me, you, him, her, it, us, them
   Please help ME.   I saw THEM.

POSSESSIVE adjectives — show who owns it (before a noun)
   my, your, his, her, its, our, their
   This is MY bag.   That is THEIR house.

POSSESSIVE pronouns — stand alone (no noun after)
   mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs
   This bag is MINE.   That house is THEIRS.

QUICK TEST
   Before the verb → subject (I, he, she)
   After the verb → object (me, him, her)
   Before a noun → my, his, her
   Standing alone → mine, his, hers
ruleZh: 代词代替名词。动词前用主格：I, he, she。动词后用宾格：me, him, her。名词前用 my, his, her。单独用 mine, his, hers。

questions.q: Replace 'Mama' with a pronoun: Mama is kind.

title: Verbs: Present Tense
rule:
A VERB is an action or a state of being.
   eat, run, sleep, cook, be, have

SIMPLE PRESENT — habits and facts
   I / You / We / They  →  base verb
      I eat rice.   They walk to school.
   He / She / It  →  add -s
      She eats rice.   He walks to school.

THE -s RULE (only for he / she / it)
   Most verbs: add -s        →  walk → walks
   Ends in -s, -sh, -ch, -x: add -es  →  watch → watches
   Consonant + y: y → -ies   →  study → studies
   Irregular: have → has,  go → goes,  do → does

NEGATIVE
   I / You / We / They  →  do not (don't)
      I do not eat fish.
   He / She / It  →  does not (doesn't)
      She does not eat fish.  (verb has NO -s here!)

QUESTIONS
   Do you eat rice?     Does she eat rice?
   (verb stays plain after do/does)

BE verb — special
   I am,  you are,  he/she/it is,  we are,  they are
ruleZh: 现在时表示习惯和事实。I/you/we/they 用动词原形；he/she/it 要加 -s。否定用 do not / does not。疑问用 Do / Does。注意：用了 does 之后动词不加 -s。

questions.q: He ___ to the market on Saturday.

title: Verbs: Past Tense
rule:
PAST TENSE — something that already happened.

REGULAR verbs: add -ed
   walk → walked,  cook → cooked,  clean → cleaned
   Ends in -e: just add -d      →  like → liked
   Consonant + y: y → -ied      →  study → studied
   Short vowel + consonant: double it  →  stop → stopped

IRREGULAR verbs — must memorise (no -ed!)
   go → went          eat → ate         drink → drank
   see → saw          come → came       give → gave
   take → took        make → made       say → said
   have → had         do → did          run → ran
   buy → bought       bring → brought   think → thought
   is/am → was        are → were

NEGATIVE — did not + base verb
   I did not go.  (NOT 'did not went')

QUESTIONS — Did + base verb
   Did you go?  (NOT 'Did you went?')

BIG RULE: after DID, the verb goes back to plain form.
ruleZh: 过去时表示已经发生的事。规则动词加 -ed。不规则动词要背（go→went, eat→ate）。否定用 did not + 动词原形。疑问用 Did + 动词原形。

title: Adjectives
rule:
An ADJECTIVE describes a noun.
   a BIG house,  a KIND woman,  DELICIOUS food

WHERE THEY GO
   Before a noun:       a green bag
   After be/seem/look:  The bag IS green.

ORDER OF ADJECTIVES (when using more than one)
   Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material
   a beautiful big old round green Chinese wooden table
   (In practice, use only two or three.)
   ✅ a lovely small red bag       ❌ a red small lovely bag

COMPARING TWO THINGS — comparative
   Short words: add -er + than     →  big → bigger than
   Ends in -y: y → -ier            →  happy → happier than
   Long words: use more            →  more beautiful than
   Irregular: good → better, bad → worse

COMPARING THREE OR MORE — superlative
   Short words: the + -est         →  the biggest
   Long words: the most            →  the most beautiful
   Irregular: good → the best, bad → the worst

NEVER double up
   ❌ more bigger    ✅ bigger
   ❌ most biggest   ✅ the biggest
ruleZh: 形容词描述名词，放在名词前或 be 动词后。比较两个用 -er/more...than；比较三个以上用 the -est/the most。不能重复：不能说 more bigger。

title: Articles: a, an, the
rule:
A / AN / THE come before nouns.

A — before a CONSONANT sound
   a cat,  a book,  a house,  a university (yoo sound!)

AN — before a VOWEL sound (a e i o u)
   an apple,  an egg,  an umbrella,  an hour (silent h!)

⚠️ It is the SOUND that matters, not the letter.
   a university (sounds like 'yoo')
   an hour (the h is silent, sounds like 'our')

THE — a specific thing both people know
   THE cat on my sofa.  (that particular cat)
   Also for: the sun, the moon, the world, the market

NO ARTICLE needed for:
   Plurals in general:  I like cats.  (not 'the cats')
   Uncountable in general: I drink water.
   Names: Singapore, Mama, English
   Meals: I eat breakfast.

A vs THE
   I saw A cat.   (any cat, first mention)
   THE cat was black.  (now we both know which cat)
ruleZh: a 用在辅音前，an 用在元音前 —— 看发音不是字母。the 指双方都知道的特定事物。复数泛指、不可数泛指、人名地名前不加冠词。

umbrella starts with a vowel sound.
The h is silent → vowel sound.

title: Prepositions
rule:
PREPOSITIONS show place, time or direction.

PLACE
   in    — inside something:  in the bag, in the room
   on    — touching a surface: on the table, on the wall
   under — below:  under the chair
   next to / beside — at the side of
   behind — at the back of
   in front of — at the front of
   between — in the middle of two things
   opposite — facing

TIME
   at  — exact time:      at 7 o'clock, at noon
   on  — days and dates:  on Monday, on 5 May
   in  — months, years, long periods: in May, in 2026, in the morning

⚠️ Special: at night (not 'in the night')

MOVEMENT
   to — towards:  I go to the market.
   from — starting point:  I came from home.
   into — entering:  She walked into the room.

COMMON MISTAKES
   ❌ I go to home      ✅ I go home
   ❌ in Monday         ✅ on Monday
   ❌ on the morning    ✅ in the morning
ruleZh: 介词表示地点、时间、方向。in 里面，on 表面，under 下面。时间：at 用于钟点，on 用于日期星期，in 用于月份年份。注意 at night。

title: Sentence Structure
rule:
Every English sentence needs a SUBJECT and a VERB.

BASIC ORDER:  SUBJECT + VERB + OBJECT
   Mama  cooks  dinner.
   I     eat    rice.
   She   loves  her family.

⚠️ English word order is fixed. You cannot move things freely like in Chinese.
   ✅ I eat rice every day.
   ❌ Every day rice I eat.

SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT
   Singular subject → singular verb:  The cat IS sleeping.
   Plural subject → plural verb:      The cats ARE sleeping.

CAPITAL LETTERS
   Start of a sentence:  She is kind.
   Names and places:     Mama, Singapore, English
   The word I:           always capital I

PUNCTUATION
   .  full stop — ends a statement
   ?  question mark — ends a question
   !  exclamation mark — strong feeling
   ,  comma — a short pause, or lists

JOINING SENTENCES
   and     — adds:        I cook AND she cleans.
   but     — contrasts:   I am tired BUT happy.
   because — gives reason: I am happy BECAUSE she came.
   so      — gives result: I was tired SO I slept.
ruleZh: 英语句子必须有主语和动词，顺序是 主语+动词+宾语，不能随意调换。单数主语配单数动词。句首和人名要大写，I 永远大写。用 and, but, because, so 连接句子。

title: Adverbs
rule:
An ADVERB describes a VERB, an adjective, or another adverb.
   She walks SLOWLY.  (how she walks)

ADJECTIVE vs ADVERB — the key difference
   Adjective describes a NOUN:   She is a QUICK walker.
   Adverb describes a VERB:      She walks QUICKLY.

MAKING ADVERBS — usually add -ly
   quick → quickly,  slow → slowly,  careful → carefully
   Ends in -y: y → -ily    →  happy → happily
   Ends in -le: drop e     →  simple → simply

IRREGULAR
   good → well  (NOT 'goodly')
   fast → fast  (no change)
   hard → hard  (no change)
   ⚠️ 'hardly' means 'almost not' — a different meaning!

TYPES
   How:       quickly, carefully, well
   When:      now, later, yesterday, soon
   How often: always, usually, often, sometimes, never
   Where:     here, there, outside

FREQUENCY ADVERBS go before the main verb
   I ALWAYS eat rice.   She NEVER drinks coffee.
   But AFTER the be verb:  She is ALWAYS happy.
ruleZh: 副词修饰动词，通常加 -ly。形容词修饰名词，副词修饰动词：She is quick（形容词）/ She walks quickly（副词）。good 的副词是 well。频率副词放在主动词前。

questions.why: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb.
'hard' means with effort. 'hardly' means almost not.
